item.title: UK reaffirms commitment to deepen defence, security partnership with Nigeria
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its longstanding defence and security partnership with Nigeria, with renewed focus on military cooperation, professional military education, institutional capacity building and enhanced operational effectiveness. Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba said the commitment was reiterated when the recently appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr. Pete Vowles, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General OO Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters, Abuja. The British High Commissioner expressed appreciation for the enduring political, diplomatic and military relations between both countries, emphasising that defence and security cooperation remain critical pillars of the UK-Nigeria bilateral relationship. He underscored his determination to sustain the momentum of existing security initiatives and explore opportunities to deepen collaboration in response to evolving regional and global security challenges. He further highlighted the importance of maintaining a strong and mutually beneficial partnership that support regional stability and strengthens Nigeria’s capacity to address contemporary security threats. In his response, the CDS highlighted the longstanding historical ties between Nigeria and the United Kingdom, noting that both countries have sustained a productive defence relationship for several decades and continued to work together in addressing shared security concerns. General Oluyede emphasised the importance of sustaining and expanding existing areas of cooperation, particularly in professional military education, transfer of technology and institutional capacity building. He noted that ongoing defence agreements and training programmes have contributed to enhancing the professional competence and operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria. The CDS stressed that continued collaboration with strategic international partners remains important to strengthening the Armed Forces’ capacity to respond effectively to emerging threats, while promoting greater self-reliance, institutional resilience and operational efficiency. Both parties expressed optimism about the future of the UK-Nigeria defence and security partnership, reaffirming their commitment to building on existing achievements and identifying further areas of cooperation for mutual benefit. item.title: Ogun Assembly backs establishment of state police
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the proposed establishment of state police, passing a resolution in support of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026. The resolution, titled “H.R. No. 194/OG/2025 – Consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999) (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 (Establishment of State Police Services),” was passed during plenary, following the consideration of a report by the House Ad-hoc Committee on Constitutional Review. The committee, chaired by a former Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Olakunle Oluomo, presented its report on 26 clauses and proposed amendments to various sections of the 1999 Constitution. Presenting the report, Oluomo took the proposed amendments one after another, with lawmakers voting in favour of all the clauses and sections contained in the proposals. The amendments covered various aspects of the bill, including the substitution, insertion and alteration of specific constitutional provisions aimed at providing a legal framework for the establishment of state police services. Following the consideration of the proposed amendments, Oluomo moved a motion for the adoption of the committee’s report. The motion was seconded by Hon. Adegoke Adeyanju and subsequently supported by the lawmakers through a voice vote. The House Leader, Hon. Yusuf Sherif, thereafter moved a motion for the adoption of the report as a resolution of the Assembly. The motion was seconded by the Chief Whip, Hon. Omolola Bakare, and unanimously supported by members through a voice vote. Speaking after the passage of the resolution, the Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Oludaisi Elemide, said the Assembly had joined other state legislatures across the country in supporting the establishment of state police, describing the decision as historic. Elemide said the resolution reflected the position of the lawmakers and the people of Ogun State on the need to strengthen the country’s security architecture through the establishment of state police services. According to him, the initiative would help improve security measures and enhance the protection of lives and property, while promoting the social well-being and economic development of the state. He added that the proposed establishment of state police was an important step towards addressing security challenges and strengthening the capacity to safeguard communities. Following the passage of the resolution, the Speaker directed that a clean copy of the document be prepared and transmitted to the National Assembly to formally communicate Ogun State’s support for the proposed constitutional amendment. The resolution forms part of the ongoing constitutional amendment process through which state legislatures are considering proposed changes to the 1999 Constitution, including the proposal to establish state police services. item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government and Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited have signed a final settlement to end a nearly 20-year dispute over MMA2, paving the way for renewed revenue generation and the completion of abandoned hotel and conference centre projects in Lagos. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during the formal signing of the agreement, saying the settlement would enable the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to begin receiving concession fees from MMA2 after years of litigation. Keyamo said the agreement followed the approval of the Federal Executive Council and the Federal Government’s decision under President Bola Tinubu to resolve the protracted dispute through negotiations rather than continued court battles. He described the settlement as a reciprocal arrangement under which both parties had agreed to relinquish outstanding claims to establish a framework for future cooperation. He noted that the resolution had been achieved without the Federal Government engaging external lawyers for the negotiations. Speaking at the event, Babalakin thanked President Tinubu and Keyamo for resolving the dispute, which he said had remained unresolved for more than 18 years despite the parties having maintained their respective positions. He said the settlement would create employment opportunities, particularly through the completion of the abandoned projects, while improving the appearance of the airport environment. According to him, the agreement would also encourage investors who have encountered disputes with government to consider negotiated solutions as a viable means of resolving disagreements. Babalakin assured the government, the ministry and FAAN that Bi-Courtney would honour its commitments under the agreement. item.title: Police rescue 11 Ghanaians lured to Nigeria with Canada visa offer
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has rescued 11 Ghanaian nationals allegedly held against their will in Sagamu, Ogun State, after being lured to Nigeria with promises of Canadian and Spanish visas in a suspected international fraud scheme involving about ₦50.27 million. The victims, comprising seven males and four females, were rescued on October 19, following intelligence received by the police, according to a statement issued on Tuesday by the Command’s Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi. The statement said operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit swiftly mobilised to the suspected hideout after receiving actionable intelligence and successfully rescued all 11 victims. Preliminary investigations, according to the police, indicated that the victims were allegedly deceived by a fellow Ghanaian national who promised to facilitate their travel abroad. Each victim reportedly paid GH₵40,000 before being brought to Nigeria, where they were allegedly held against their will. However, the Command said investigations were ongoing to identify, track down and apprehend everyone connected with the alleged criminal network. The rescued Ghanaian nationals are receiving appropriate care and support, while detectives intensify efforts to unravel the circumstances surrounding their alleged ordeal. Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, commended operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit for their prompt response and professionalism. Ojajuni reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives, combating transnational crime and preventing criminal networks from exploiting unsuspecting members of the public. He declared that the state would not provide a safe haven for individuals who prey on the hopes and trust of others. “There is no safe haven for criminals who exploit the hopes of others,” the police commissioner said. He assured residents and members of the public that the Command would sustain its efforts to ensure that those responsible for the alleged crime were brought to justice. The Command urged members of the public to exercise caution when dealing with individuals or agents offering overseas travel and visa-processing services. It advised prospective travellers to verify the authenticity of travel arrangements and the credentials of service providers before making payments. The police also encouraged the public to report suspicious activities that could help security agencies identify and disrupt criminal operations. Reiterating its commitment to intelligence-led policing and effective collaboration with other security agencies, the Command said it would continue to take decisive action against criminal networks operating within the state. “Every credible lead matters, every life matters, and protecting the public remains paramount,” the statement added. item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State House of Assembly, on Tuesday, threw its weight behind the creation of state police, passing the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, with all 22 members present voting in favour and none against, as lawmakers pushed for a decentralised policing system to tackle insecurity. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent from plenary during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in the country. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to supporting constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. He stressed that implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, argued that policing must be brought closer to the people. He said a decentralised system would sharpen security responses and address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies, to ensure the proposed State Police Services complement existing security structures and improve overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, insisted on adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect the fundamental rights of citizens. Lawmakers also cited improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as key benefits of a decentralised policing system. The passage marks the Assembly’s formal endorsement of the proposed amendments, paving the way for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. item.title: Tambuwal dismisses APC defection rumours
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO: Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he plans to defect from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the claims as false and misleading. The former Sokoto State governor, through his media office, said he had no intention of leaving the ADC, warning that the speculation could create unnecessary confusion ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement dated October 19, 2026, and signed by Prince Daniel, Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to the senator, Tambuwal’s media office reaffirmed his commitment to the ADC and its political objectives. “For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Tambuwal has no plans to join the APC. Suggestions to the contrary are false, baseless and should be disregarded,” the statement said. The clarification comes amid heightened political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 elections, as parties and their leading figures position themselves for the contest. However, the media office insisted that the reports should not be interpreted as an indication of any impending change in Tambuwal’s party affiliation. It explained that the senator’s longstanding relationships with politicians across party lines should not be misconstrued as evidence of a planned defection, noting that his years in public service had enabled him to maintain friendships and political contacts beyond the ADC. item.title: Governance will suffer if Tinubu campaigns nationwide — Ex-Obidient Chief

Ngogbehei, a former coordinator of the Obidient Movement, also challenged critics of the removal of the petrol subsidy to an open debate on the policy, urging them to offer alternatives that take Nigeria’s economic realities into account. He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja alongside the National Coordinator of the movement, Engr. Ibrahim Said Uba, during a media parley where he explained why the President might not personally attend campaign activities in every state. “One of the greatest challenges we are having in this country is the time to govern and the time to do electioneering,” Ngogbehei said. He argued that the early commencement of political mobilisation for subsequent elections had undermined governance, with political actors shifting attention away from delivering on their mandates. “A president gets into office, and one year after he gets into office, they start preparing for the next election. And what suffers? Governance suffers,” he said. According to him, Tinubu has chosen to delegate campaign responsibilities to trusted associates to enable him to concentrate on governance. “The President has said, ‘I want to focus on governance. Challenges critics to subsidy debate On the removal of the petrol subsidy, Ngogbehei invited critics of the policy to a public discussion on the rationale behind the decision and the alternatives available to the government. He said participants should examine the challenges the policy was intended to address and assess whether alternative approaches could deliver better outcomes. “We are telling the person, let us sit down and let us x-ray these things. “You need to first of all show us that you understand the problem and then, if you were there, what would you do differently, putting into consideration all the complexities of Nigeria?” he asked. Ngogbehei said the invitation was open to individuals and groups, regardless of their political affiliations. “We are open to have this discussion with anyone, anytime, any day. Let us just be open, let us be transparent, let us be factual. It is our country. We cannot run it by propaganda. We cannot run it by lies,” he said. Borrowing would have worsened situation — Uba In his remarks, Uba warned that continued borrowing to sustain the subsidy regime could have exposed the country to more severe fiscal difficulties. He said Nigerians had been warned that maintaining the policy could eventually undermine the government’s ability to meet obligations, including the payment of salaries. Uba described the subsidy removal as a bold decision, while acknowledging that it had imposed short-term hardship on Nigerians. “You might not like him, but he has made a bold and courageous move for the betterment of this country. Do those moves have immediate, short-term impact? Yes,” he said. He urged Nigerians to consider whether the country should bear the economic adjustment costs in the present or leave a potentially heavier burden for future generations. “Is it going to happen in our generation, or does it happen in our children’s generation when it would have been worse?” he asked. Uba said the movement wanted a balanced assessment of the economic situation inherited by the Tinubu administration, the policies introduced and their potential long-term implications. “The Tinubu Must Stay movement is saying, come, let us have a sincere, honest, transparent, and factual analysis of what he met, what he has done, the short-term impact, and what the possible long-term implications are for the country,” he said. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, for consideration and approval. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services alongside the Federal Police Service as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. Presenting the committee’s report, its chairman and member representing Qua’an-Pan South Constituency, Theodore Maiyaki, said the proposed amendment was necessary in view of prevailing security challenges, manpower shortages in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen policing at the grassroots. He explained that the proposal would establish a framework for federal and state policing, with safeguards for human rights, operational standards, accountability and coordination. The committee also noted that improved security was critical to the socioeconomic development of Plateau State and the country at large, recommending that the House support the proposed constitutional alteration. Following deliberations, lawmakers adopted the recommendations and voted in support of the proposed amendment. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, commended the committee for its work and thanked members for their patience, commitment and sacrifice in considering the legislative proposal. The constitutional amendment requires approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly before it can proceed to the next stage of the process. Meanwhile, the House passed two other bills for first reading: the Plateau State Right of Patients and Medical Institutions Bill and the Plateau State Bill on Jungle Justice, Mob Action and Other Forms of Unlawful Violence Against Persons. The bills will undergo further legislative consideration in line with the rules of the Assembly. The House subsequently resolved to proceed on recess from Monday, October 19, to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, to allow members to rest and prepare for upcoming legislative responsibilities. The Speaker appreciated lawmakers, supporting staff, and other personnel for their dedication to the service of Plateau State, noting that the Assembly had continued its legislative duties beyond the initially scheduled recess period.
